title: introduce proportional burst-degradation-controller to smooth fleet-wide burst drains
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: When the fleet experiences simultaneous transient pressure (node failures, region congestion, or unexpected warmpool exhaustion) the current burst admission policy aggressively rejects or hard-throttles burst requests which causes capacity cliffs for many tenants and regresses soft throughput guarantees for committed customers. This PR introduces a Proportional Burst-Degradation Controller (PBDC) that gracefully degrades best-effort burst capacity across eligible tenants in proportion to their recent burst consumption and SLA class, preserving committed throughput for high-tier tenants while avoiding binary hard-failures for everyone else.

What this changes: Adds a controller in the autoscaler plane that watches fleet utilization, warmpool headroom, and per-tenant burst ledgers. When the controller detects a rapid decline in available burst capacity it computes a proportional degradation vector that: 1) honors per-tenant minimum committed throughput (reservation floor), 2) uses a time-decayed recent-burst score to distribute remaining burst capacity, and 3) enforces a global safety floor to avoid starving system-critical background jobs. The controller publishes a compact policy blob to the gateway/allocator that is evaluated at request admission time.

Key behaviours: - Smooth decay: Degradation is applied over a short smoothing window (configurable, default 30s) to avoid sudden cliffing. - Tier-aware weighting: Tenants with higher reservation tiers get multiplicative priority but never exceed configured headroom caps. - Backfill safety: Opportunistic backfill requests (best-effort) are reduced proportionally before impacting reserved throughput. - Telemetry hooks: Emits proportional_degrader.summary, per-tenant.degraded_fraction_pct, and headroom_repartition events for downstream dashboards and alerts.

Tests and validation: Unit tests for the degradation allocator, scheduler integration tests exercising the gateway admission code path, and an e2e scenario that simulates a 25% sudden warmpool loss with 50 concurrent tenants. Performance microbench: controller loop 2.3ms median CPU time, and policy blob serialization < 1ms at 2000 tenants.

Operational notes: Feature gated behind runtime feature flag "proportionalBurstDegrader" and enabled in canary only. Default config conservative: smoothing_window=30s, min_committed_floor_pct=90, safety_floor=5% of global capacity. Runbook doc added.

Related: builds on prior utilization reporting work ENG-1680 (telemetry sampling) and coordinates with SUP-4123 incident postmortem to avoid repeated cliff events.
